title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: Only one past hot week with data (2025-09-08, x1.26), but this is more extreme. No prior heatwave in Nov in Austin. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk to x1.08, but heat is rare and strong—justified for 25% uplift as a conservative estimate.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 24.7. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is up 4.1% (13.93 vs 13.38), which historically has no observed lift. However, the planner notes a heatwave forecast at 38°C—unusually hot for late November in Austin. While the product has no past sales data in such heat, the 2025-09-08 promotion (30% off, 68 units, x1.26) occurred in a hot week, and the 2026-08-03 back-to-school week (x1.68) had both promotion and heat. The noise-adjusted effect of heat is uncertain (only one past hot week with data), so we shrink toward 1.0. The classical model suggests no uplift, but judgment overrides it here due to the extreme heat. We apply a moderate, uncertain upside.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 24.7 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 68.3 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 46.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
